name: Finance & economics
description: Plain-language ideas about markets, money, and the long game of investing.
sentences: A diversified portfolio spreads risk across many assets so no single loss can sink it.
Compound interest is often called the closest thing to magic in all of finance.
Inflation quietly erodes the value of cash left sitting idle in a drawer.
The stock market can stay irrational far longer than most investors can stay solvent.
Central banks raise interest rates to cool an economy that is running too hot.
A bond is simply a loan that pays the holder a fixed stream of interest.
Past performance is no guarantee of future returns, as every prospectus reminds us.
Dollar cost averaging turns market swings into a steady and almost boring habit.
Gross domestic product, or GDP, measures the total value of what a country produces.
Supply and demand set prices long before any committee gets a chance to.
Time in the market usually beats trying to time the market.
A recession is often defined as two straight quarters of shrinking output.
Fees look small on paper but can quietly consume decades of hard won gains.
An emergency fund of three to six months of expenses buys real peace of mind.
Volatility is the price of admission for the higher returns that stocks can offer.
A 2% management fee may sound trivial until you compound it over 30 years.
Cash flow keeps a business alive even when the profit line looks perfectly healthy.
The best time to start investing was years ago; the second best time is today.
A budget is just a plan that tells your money where to go before it disappears.
Markets reward patience and punish the urge to check the balance every hour.
